- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment >0.7.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, forecast often overshoots; cap peak at 1.2x recent high or 1.5x 14-day moving average.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts rise, it often overcorrects; if sentiment <0.3, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and recent price is trending down; if sentiment is 0.5–0.6, add 2–4% to forecast to avoid mean reversion trap.
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days show high values with low sentiment, model is likely overfitting; apply downward bias of 3–7% for next 7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 70% of forecast, sentiment was likely bullish but market corrected; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 10 days if sentiment remains high.
- If sentiment is high but price drops sharply after forecast peak, model is lagging; adjust forecast to match recent 7-day low if sentiment >0.67 and price drops >3% from peak.
